title: Struct aggregate initialization
recap: Aggregate initialization supplies member values in declaration order. Braces express a complete value directly and can help avoid uninitialized member state.
Returning a newly constructed aggregate keeps a transformation separate from mutation. Check both coordinates, because swapped initializer order can still compile.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement translated(point,dx,dy), returning a new Point with x+dx and y+dy. The caller's point is unchanged. Use aggregate initialization for the returned Point and keep member order in mind. Coordinates and sums fit int.
hints: Add dx to x and dy to y.
Return a Point aggregate in x,y order.
Do not reuse x for both result fields.
